Bernanke meeting with United States President [Barack Obama](/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama").

Bernanke taught at the [Stanford Graduate School of Business](/wiki/Stanford_Graduate_School_of_Business "Stanford Graduate School of Business") from 1979 until 1985, was a visiting professor at [New York University](/wiki/New_York_University "New York University") and went on to become a [tenured](/wiki/Tenure "Tenure") professor at [Princeton University](/wiki/Princeton_University "Princeton University") in the [Department of Economics](/wiki/Princeton_University_Department_of_Economics "Princeton University Department of Economics"). He chaired that department from 1996 until September 2002, when he went on public service leave. He resigned his position at Princeton on July 1, 2005.

Bernanke served as a member of the [Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System](/wiki/Board_of_Governors_of_the_Federal_Reserve_System "Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System") from 2002 to 2005. fanoutqa_033204.x:
Eiffel Tower :: History :: Inauguration and the 1889 exposition :: chunk_0008
[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/72/Exposition_Universelle_de_Paris_1889_-_Universit%C3%A4ts-_und_Landesbibliothek_Darmstadt.jpg/250px-Exposition_Universelle_de_Paris_1889_-_Universit%C3%A4ts-_und_Landesbibliothek_Darmstadt.jpg)](/wiki/File:Exposition_Universelle_de_Paris_1889_-_Universit%C3%A4ts-_und_Landesbibliothek_Darmstadt.jpg)

View of the 1889 World's Fair

The main structural work was completed at the end of March 1889 and, on 31 March, Eiffel celebrated by leading a group of government officials, accompanied by representatives of the press, to the top of the tower.[[20]](#cite_note-times1_4_89-20) Because the lifts were not yet in operation, the ascent was made by foot, and took over an hour, with Eiffel stopping frequently to explain various features. Most of the party chose to stop at the lower levels, but a few, including the structural engineer, Émile Nouguier, the head of construction, Jean Compagnon, the President of the City Council, and reporters from *[Le Figaro](/wiki/Le_Figaro "Le Figaro")* and *[Le Monde Illustré](/wiki/Le_Monde_Illustr%C3%A9 "Le Monde Illustré")*, completed the ascent. At 2:35 pm, Eiffel hoisted a large [Tricolour](/wiki/Flag_of_France "Flag of France") to the accompaniment of a 25-gun salute fired at the first level.[[30]](#cite_note-30)

There was still work to be done, particularly on the lifts and facilities, and the tower was not opened to the public until nine days after the opening of the exposition on 6 May; even then, the lifts had not been completed. The tower was an instant success with the public, and nearly 30,000 visitors made the 1,710-step climb to the top before the lifts entered service on 26 May.[[31]](#cite_note-Exposition-31) Tickets cost 2 francs for the first level, 3 for the second, and 5 for the top, with half-price admission on Sundays,[[32]](#cite_note-32) and by the end of the exhibition there had been

fanoutqa_021428.t: Helium :: History :: Scientific discoveries :: part 01 :: chunk_0005
fanoutqa_021428.x:
Helium :: History :: Scientific discoveries :: part 01 :: chunk_0005
The first evidence of helium was observed on August 18, 1868, as a bright yellow line with a [wavelength](/wiki/Wavelength "Wavelength") of 587.49 nanometers in the [spectrum](/wiki/Emission_spectrum "Emission spectrum") of the [chromosphere](/wiki/Chromosphere "Chromosphere") of the [Sun](/wiki/Sun "Sun"). The line was detected by French astronomer [Jules Janssen](/wiki/Pierre_Janssen "Pierre Janssen") during [a total solar eclipse](/wiki/Solar_eclipse_of_August_18,_1868 "Solar eclipse of August 18, 1868") in [Guntur](/wiki/Guntur "Guntur"), India.[[26]](#cite_note-frnch-27)[[27]](#cite_note-nbb-28) This line was initially assumed to be [sodium](/wiki/Sodium "Sodium"). On October 20 of the same year, English astronomer [Norman Lockyer](/wiki/Norman_Lockyer "Norman Lockyer") observed a yellow line in the solar spectrum, which he named the D3 because it was near the known D1 and D2 [Fraunhofer lines](/wiki/Fraunhofer_line "Fraunhofer line") of sodium.[[28]](#cite_note-Lockyer_1868-29)[[29]](#cite_note-enc-30) He concluded that it was caused by an element in the Sun unknown on Earth. Lockyer named the element helium, from the Greek word for the Sun, [ἥλιος](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/en:%E1%BC%A5%CE%BB%CE%B9%CE%BF%CF%82 "wikt:en:ἥλιος") (*[helios](/wiki/Helios "Helios")*).[[30]](#cite_note-31)[[31]](#cite_note-32) It is sometimes said that English chemist [Edward Frankland](/wiki/Edward_Frankland "Edward Frankland") was also involved in the naming, but this is unlikely as he doubted the existence of this new element. The ending "-ium" is unusual, as it normally applies only to metallic elements; probably Lockyer, being an astronomer, was unaware of the chemical conventions.[[32]](#cite_note-jensen-33)

The concept of a forum for the capitalist world's major [industrialized countries](/wiki/Industrialized_countries "Industrialized countries") emerged before the [1973 oil crisis](/wiki/1973_oil_crisis "1973 oil crisis"). On 25 March 1973, the [United States secretary of the treasury](/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_the_Treasury "United States Secretary of the Treasury"), [George Shultz](/wiki/George_Shultz "George Shultz"), convened an informal gathering of [finance ministers](/wiki/Finance_ministers "Finance ministers") from West Germany ([Helmut Schmidt](/wiki/Helmut_Schmidt "Helmut Schmidt")), France ([Valéry Giscard d'Estaing](/wiki/Val%C3%A9ry_Giscard_d%27Estaing "Valéry Giscard d'Estaing")), and the United Kingdom ([Anthony Barber](/wiki/Anthony_Barber "Anthony Barber")) before an upcoming meeting in [Washington, DC](/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C."). United States president [Richard Nixon](/wiki/Richard_M._Nixon "Richard M. Nixon") offered the [White House](/wiki/White_House "White House") as a venue, and the meeting was subsequently held in [its library](/wiki/White_House_Library "White House Library") on the ground floor;[[15]](#cite_note-Schultz-15) the original group of four consequently became known as the "Library Group".[[16]](#cite_note-16) In mid-1973, at the Spring Meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, Shultz proposed the addition of Japan, which all members accepted.[[15]](#cite_note-Schultz-15) The informal gathering of senior financial officials from the United States, United Kingdom, [West Germany](/wiki/West_Germany "West Germany"), Japan, and France became known as the "Group of Five".[[17]](#cite_note-17)

In 1974, all five members endured sudden and often troubled changes in leadership. French president [Georges Pompidou](/wiki/Georges_Pompidou "Georges Pompidou") abruptly died, leading to a [fresh presidential election](/wiki/1974_French_presidential_election "1974 F

The 2019 World Championship was held between 2 October to 10 November 2019, in three countries and cities in [Europe](/wiki/Europe "Europe"): [Berlin](/wiki/Berlin "Berlin") (play-in & groups), [Madrid](/wiki/Madrid "Madrid") (quarterfinals and semifinals), and [Paris](/wiki/Paris "Paris") (final).[[46]](#cite_note-47) Twenty-four teams qualified to participate at the World Championship based on placement within their own regional leagues and previous regional results in international play.[[47]](#cite_note-48)

The 2019 World Championship was played on Patch 9.19 from start to finish.[[48]](#cite_note-49) The World Championship final was played on 10 November 2019 between [LPL](/wiki/League_of_Legends_Pro_League "League of Legends Pro League")'s [FunPlus Phoenix](/wiki/FunPlus_Phoenix "FunPlus Phoenix") and [LEC](/wiki/League_of_Legends_European_Championship "League of Legends European Championship")'s [G2 Esports](/wiki/G2_Esports "G2 Esports") at [AccorHotels Arena](/wiki/AccorHotels_Arena "AccorHotels Arena") in Paris. FunPlus Phoenix won 3–0 against G2 Esports, granting China and the LPL back-to-back World Championships. Gao "Tian" Tianliang was named the MVP of the series in their victory.[[49]](#cite_note-50) The final was watched by more than 100 million viewers, peaking at 44 million concurrent views.[[50]](#cite_note-51)

**Thomas Jefferson** (April 13 [[O.S.](/wiki/Old_Style_and_New_Style_dates "Old Style and New Style dates") April 2], 1743 – July 4, 1826) was a [Founding Father](/wiki/Founding_Father_of_the_United_States "Founding Father of the United States"), second [vice president](/wiki/Vice_president_of_the_United_States "Vice president of the United States"), and third [president of the United States](/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") from 1801 to 1809.[[3]](#cite_note-Morris19732-4) Jefferson was the primary author of the [Declaration of Independence](/wiki/United_States_Declaration_of_Independence "United States Declaration of Independence"). He was a leading proponent of [democracy](/wiki/Democracy "Democracy"), [republicanism](/wiki/Republicanism_in_the_United_States "Republicanism in the United States"), and [natural rights](/wiki/Natural_law "Natural law"), and produced formative documents and decisions at the state, national, and international levels.

Jefferson was born into the [Colony of Virginia](/wiki/Colony_of_Virginia "Colony of Virginia")'s [planter class](/wiki/Planter_class "Planter class"). During the [American Revolution](/wiki/American_Revolution "American Revolution"), he represented Virginia in the [Second Continental Congress](/wiki/Second_Continental_Congress "Second Continental Congress"), which unanimously adopted the Declaration of Independence. Jefferson's advocacy for [individual rights](/wiki/Individual_and_group_rights "Individual and group rights"), including [freedom of thought](/wiki/Freedom_of_thought "Freedom of thought"), [speech](/wiki/Freedom_of_speech "Freedom of speech"), and [religion](/wiki/Freedom_of_religion "Freedom of religion"), helped shape the ideological foundations of the revolution.[[4]](#cite_note-5)[[5]](#cite_note-6) Jefferson served as the second [governor of Virginia](/wiki/Governor_of_Virginia "Governor of Virginia") from 1779 to 1781. Main article: [2022 FIFA World Cup final](/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_final "2022 FIFA World Cup final")

The final was played on 18 December between Argentina and France. Both teams had won the event twice previously.[[227]](#cite_note-final1-248) Early goals from Lionel Messi and [Ángel Di María](/wiki/%C3%81ngel_Di_Mar%C3%ADa "Ángel Di María") gave Argentina a 2–0 lead against the French.[[227]](#cite_note-final1-248)[[228]](#cite_note-final2-249) Despite substitutions in the first half, France did not record a shot until after the 70th minute but were energised by additional substitutions in the 71st. A few minutes later, France were awarded a penalty as [Randal Kolo Muani](/wiki/Randal_Kolo_Muani "Randal Kolo Muani") was brought down in the penalty area by [Nicolás Otamendi](/wiki/Nicol%C3%A1s_Otamendi "Nicolás Otamendi"). Mbappé scored the penalty and added a second goal less than two minutes later to equalise the scores.[[228]](#cite_note-final2-249) With the score tied at two goals apiece, the match went to extra time. Messi scored his second goal in the 108th minute, once again giving Argentina the lead. However, Mbappé was awarded a second penalty in the 115th minute after his shot hit the arm of [Gonzalo Montiel](/wiki/Gonzalo_Montiel "Gonzalo Montiel"). Mbappé scored his third goal, becoming the second player ever to complete a [hat-trick](/wiki/Hat-trick "Hat-trick") in the final of a World Cup after [Geoff Hurst](/wiki/Geoff_Hurst "Geoff Hurst") for England in [1966](/wiki/1966_FIFA_World_Cup "1966 FIFA World Cup").[[228]](#cite_note-final2-249) With the score tied at 3–3, the match was determined via a penalty shootout. Argentina won the final after scoring all of their penalties, winning 4–2.[[228]](#cite_note-final2-249) This marked their third World Cup win and their first since [1986](/wiki/1986_FIFA_World_Cup "1986 FIFA World Cup"), and also the second team (after [Spain](/wiki/Spain_nati

Few were confident in the film's box office prospects. It was released in a small number of theaters in the United States on May 25, 1977, and quickly became a surprise blockbuster, leading to it being expanded to a much wider release. *Star Wars* opened to critical acclaim, with particular praise for its special effects. It grossed $410 million worldwide during its initial run, surpassing *[Jaws](/wiki/Jaws_(film) "Jaws (film)")* (1975) to become the [highest-grossing film](/wiki/Timeline_of_highest-grossing_films "Timeline of highest-grossing films") until the release of *[E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial](/wiki/E.T._the_Extra-Terrestrial "E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial")* (1982); subsequent releases have brought its total gross to $775 million. When adjusted for inflation, *Star Wars* is the [second-highest-grossing film in North America](/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_films_in_the_United_States_and_Canada#Adjusted_for_ticket-price_inflation "List of highest-grossing films in the United States and Canada") (behind *[Gone with the Wind](/wiki/Gone_with_the_Wind_(film) "Gone with the Wind (film)")*) and the [fourth-highest-grossing film of all time](/wiki/Highest-grossing_films_adjusted_for_inflation "Highest-grossing films adjusted for inflation"). It received six [Academy Awards](/wiki/50th_Academy_Awards "50th Academy Awards"), two [BAFTA](/wiki/BAFTA "BAFTA") Awards, and thirteen [Saturn Awards](/wiki/Saturn_Awards "Saturn Awards"), among others. The film has been reissued many times with Lucas' support, including the 1981 reissue giving the film the subtitle *Episode IV – A New Hope*, and the 1997 "Special Edition". The reissues have contained many changes, including new scenes, visual effects, and dialogue.
